advances: Ordinary triangle caps at the endpoint of the strict incidence theorem. The counterexample concerns including the endpoint in that incidence implication.
author: PK-research-agent
proof:
Put $s=\sqrt3$, $x=(s-1)/2$, and $z=(3-s)/4$. The point $p$ with barycentric coordinates $(x,z,z)$ is interior since all three coordinates are positive and $x+2z=1$. Let $\lambda_i$ be the barycentric coordinate functions of the three vertices. Define the affine margins
$$
f_1=(s/2)\lambda_1-\lambda_3,\qquad
f_2=-x\lambda_1+\lambda_2-\lambda_3/s,\qquad
f_3=-x\lambda_1-\lambda_2/s+\lambda_3.
$$
Use the halfspaces $H_i=\{w:f_i(w)\ge0\}$. The identities $(s/2)x=z$ and $x^2=z(1-1/s)$ give $f_i(p)=0$ for every $i$. Since $x(1+1/s)=s/3$ and $1/s^2=1/3$, the coefficient of each $\lambda_j$ in $(2/3)f_1+f_2/s+f_3$ is zero. This supplies a positive dependence of the gradients. The first two gradients are independent: if proportional, the corresponding margins would be proportional because both vanish at $p$, but $f_1(P_2)=0$ and $f_2(P_2)=1$. Thus the gradients span the plane.

The first margin has vertex values $(s/2,0,-1)$. The cap is the triangle at $P_1$ with edge-intercept fractions $1$ and $s/(s+2)$, so its area fraction is $s/(s+2)=2s-3$. The second margin has vertex values $(-x,1,-1/s)$. Its cap is the triangle at $P_2$ with edge-intercept fractions $1/(1+x)=2x$ and $1/(1+1/s)=2z$, both strictly between zero and one. Its area fraction is $4xz=2s-3$. Interchanging $P_2,P_3$ gives the same calculation for the third cap. These are actual caps on the specified triangle, including the boundary incidence of the first one.
statement: In any nondegenerate planar triangle with vertices $P_1,P_2,P_3$, there is an interior point $p$ and three closed through-$p$ caps whose normals span the plane and admit a strictly positive linear dependence, each of ordinary area fraction $2\sqrt3-3$, such that the first cap strictly captures $P_1$ and contains $P_2$ on its cutting line. Thus the strict incidence conclusion at smaller ceilings can fail at the threshold.
title: A positive-circuit triangle cap with a boundary vertex at the sharp ceiling
